messages:
incident-bot: ALERT p99 spike detected on /v1/chat/completions (route: chat-completions, model: open-m-3) — p99 = 2.8s, baseline 1.1s. paging @oncall/eng-sre
alex: oncall here — saw it. I'm going to page a mitigation and start triage. Any customer 5xxs?
sam: no 5xx trends, but tail latency correlates with payload size spikes from SSO service around the same window.
tara: dropping in — can we shard traffic to dedicated pool for chat-completions while we dig? We have capacity in dedicated-2.
alex: good call. @console-bot can we route route=chat-completions to pool=dedicated-2 for the next 15m? /incident assign @alex
console-bot: routing change applied: route=chat-completions -> dedicated-2 (transient 15m). logs: https://console.redwood.ai/routediff/1767412345
mike: deploying the temporary routing now. Also will flip to smaller model variant open-m-3-small for non-SL tier to reduce cost and latency.
eva: tagging customer-impact: a small fraction of requests to a few enterprise customers saw degraded response times (login flows slow). I raised a priority-2 customer ticket.
alex: mitigation in flight. while that runs, we should silence noisy p99 alerts that are firing for routes we already have mitigations for. propose: squelch p99 alerts for chat-completions for 30m and create a follow-up for tuning.
sam: +1. also let's add a temporary dashboard with model-level p95/p99 per route so we can see regressions across variants.
tara: I'll make the dashboard. provisional PromQL for the panel: ```
quantile_over_time(0.99, job:request_latency_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/chat/completions",model=~"open-m-3.*"}[5m])
```
alex: nice. For alert tuning, propose new thresholds while we investigate: p95=0.9s, p99=1.8s (was 1.4s global p99) but scoped per-model-per-route. we need to avoid masking real regressions.
mike: let's version the alert rules. example alert change: ```
- alert: ChatCompletions_P99_OpenM3
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket{route=\"chat-completions\",model=\"open-m-3\"}[5m])) by (le)) > 1.8
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    runbook: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/chat-completions-p99
```
eva: make sure we tag suppressed alerts with `incident=1767412345` so we can reconcile. customers need a clean timeline.
sam: agreed. also add a correlating panel for SSO latency to validate the dependency theory.
tara: dashboard up: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/d-9k2rt - includes per-route/per-model p95/p99, request size histogram, and upstream sso latency.
alex: customer message draft: "We observed increased response times impacting a subset of users, mitigations applied by routing traffic and model fallback; monitoring indicates service returning to baseline. Follow-up: tuning alert thresholds and creating per-model dashboards". anybody edit?
eva: looks good, add ETA for postmortem: 48h with concrete tuning plan.
mike: ops note: we should consider adding an automated fallback policy for when p99 exceeds 1.6x baseline: auto-route to dedicated pool + smaller variant. I'll open a ticket.
sam: logged ENGOPS-4123 "auto-fallback policy for chat-completions p99 spikes" and linked to this incident.
alex: ok wrapping up: keep squelch for 30m, dashboard is live, alert rule PR opened (ENGOPS-4124). please add any additional customer notes into the ticket. if latency climbs again, we'll escalate to full incident.
incident-bot: INCIDENT 1767412345 status: mitigated -> monitoring. duration: 00:37:15. pages: 1. linked tickets: ENGOPS-4123, ENGOPS-4124.
eva: post-incident actions: (1) split p95/p99 alerts per-model/per-route, (2) add a 10m hysteresis window to reduce noise, (3) run a 24h replay of the traffic spike on staging to validate thresholds. adding owners: sam (alerts), mike (fallbacks), tara (dashboards).
alex: thanks all. I'll hand this off to follow-up owners. closing thread in 1h unless new activity. :white_check_mark:
